title: Always love heading to ATL to visit @Alliance Theatre #regionaltheatr...
transcript: Welcome to a regional theatre spotlight. Today we are heading to Atlanta, Georgia to check out the world premiere of water for elephants at the Alliance Theatre, located in the Arts District of Atlanta. The Alliance Theatre continuously produces some of my favorite seasons. A nice mix of world premieres, award winners, and a good roster of theatre for young audiences. You've produced some of your favorite shows, including ride the Cyclone, The Prom, The Color Purple. Last year I saw Trading Places in this space, which I absolutely loved, so I had to come back to see water for elephants, another world premiere musical. The alliance is a recipient of the Regional Theatre Tony Award that they won in 2007 after The Color Purple went to Broadway. They also renovated the space in 2019 and it is stunning and some of the most comfortable chairs I've ever sat in in a theater. Water for elephants is their last show of this season. It closes July 9th. My full thoughts are coming shortly, but if you are in Atlanta, I cannot recommend subscribing to their next season enough. It is stunning fact there are so many exciting new plays coming next season, including the world premiere of the Preachers Wife musical and a ton of my favorite plays from last year, including English and a production of Fat Ham directed by Stevie Walker web. I cannot wait!
